# Crypto Lab

> A catalog of 252 browser-based cryptography teaching demos ("labs"), each a
> static single-page site with its own repository, published at
> https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/

Crypto Lab exists to teach cryptography honestly: every lab states what is real
versus simulated, what it does NOT prove, and that it is a teaching demo rather
than production cryptography. The catalog carries machine-checked evidence for
each lab's claims — every credited algorithm has a `file:line` anchor into that
lab's own source, and a claim without one fails the catalog's own checks.

## Audit corpus

For auditing or analysing every lab from one fetch, use the generated corpus
rather than crawling the site or cloning 252 repositories. Each record pins the
commit its content was read from, so findings stay checkable.

- [corpus/index.json](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/corpus/index.json): lab count, per-category and per-level counts, clones behind their remote, and every lab with missing fields. Start here.
- [corpus/labs.jsonl](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/corpus/labs.jsonl): one JSON record per lab — hero text, category, level, accent, derived algorithms with source anchors, spec citations as written, full README, asserted claims with their expected values, mutation records, stated limitations.
- [corpus/index.md](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/corpus/index.md): navigation, and the command that assembles one document when the prose is sharded. It is an index and says so.
- [corpus/labs-full.md](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/corpus/labs-full.md): the prose form, with a stable heading per lab. Present only when it really holds the content; when the prose exceeds 4 MB the category shards carry it instead and this file is absent. The prose carries each README's first section and a link; the full README text is in labs.jsonl.
- [corpus/README.md](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/corpus/README.md): the schema, and the three rules for using it.

Three things to know before reporting a finding:

1. Cite `commit_sha` + lab `slug` + field. Labs move; a finding without a commit cannot be rechecked.
2. `commit_sha` is the commit the bytes were read from, not the branch tip. If `commits_behind_remote` is above zero, the lab may already be ahead of the record.
3. A field marked `MISSING` means the generator did not find it — not that the lab lacks it. Every field that was found names the file it came from, in `sources`.

## Catalog

- [index.html](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/): the catalog itself, and the single source of truth every other view is derived from.
- [CATALOG.md](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/CATALOG.md): the algorithm-level reverse index — which labs implement ML-KEM, which standards bodies are covered, where two labs overlap.
- [concept-coverage.md](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/concept-coverage.md): the catalog mapped onto about 40 concepts, and the remaining gaps.
- [README.md](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/README.md): learning paths and the full demo table.
- [knowledge-map/catalog.json](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/knowledge-map/catalog.json): exhibits, concepts, paths and modules as a graph.

## Optional

- [teach/](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/teach/): worksheets and APA citations per exhibit.
- [games/](https://crypto-lab.systemslibrarian.dev/games/): eight learning games, deliberately not part of the exhibit catalog or any derived view.
